scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it. The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1967 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Col de l Iseran → Col du Galibier
scenicChapters.narrative: Height already gained and held. The road stays near 2764 m for 143 km instead of surrendering it to the next valley — exposed ground: wind matters more here than gradient. Nothing blocks it.

scenicChapters.title: Col d Izoard → Col de Vars
scenicChapters.narrative: 70 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

scenicChapters.title: Route des Grandes Alpes
scenicChapters.narrative: A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not. The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 62 km. 607 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall.

route-des-grandes-alpes-thonon-les-bains.story: A one-way ride of 655 km, Thonon-les-Bains to Saint-Étienne-de-Tinée - roughly 9 h 09 in the saddle. It goes by way of Col des Gets, Col des Aravis, Col du Cormet de Roselend and Col de l Iseran. The highest point is about 2,750 m. Cormet de Roselend, Col du Galibier, Col d Izoard, Col de Vars and Col de Restefond are subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
